comments.body:
=== FIX IMPLEMENTED AND MUTATION-CHECKED. Gerrit 1232 (stacked on 1231, the diagnosis). ===

THE FIX, as proposed and signed off — plumb the canonical identity, do NOT relax the guard:
  * `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local:185-201` — when it emits an `assignee` change it now
    also forwards `jira_mapped["assignee_identity"]`. The mapper already computes it
    (`inbound_fields:225`), so there is no new extraction, and `account_id` already holds the
    accountId on Cloud and the username on DC (`_identity_of:154-179`, 5f48's precedence).
  * `apply_inbound_records:374` — keys the mint on that identity,
    `fields.get("assignee_identity") or fields["assignee"]`. The raw-object fallback keeps a
    caller that BYPASSES the differ (still passing the Jira user object) byte-for-byte unchanged.
  * `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:107-122` — reads `account_id` AFTER `accountId`/`name`,
    and falls back to `display` for the human-readable name.
The `isinstance(assignee, dict)` guard is untouched. A bare string still mints nothing, and
that is now pinned by a test rather than being an accident.

INERT FOR EVENT WRITING: `_inbound_update_write_edit_event` builds its EDIT from an explicit
field list (`_scalar_transforms`), so the extra key writes no extra ticket field. Verified by
the suites below, not by reading alone.

RED -> GREEN AT BOTH BOUNDARIES (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py).
Both were seen RED before the fix, each naming its own mechanism:
  * DIFFER — "the inbound differ emitted an assignee change WITHOUT `assignee_identity`, so the
    applier has only the scalar string to mint from and the mint no-ops (bug 8d68)", with
    `assert 'assignee_identity' in {'title': '', 'assignee': 'admin'}`.
  * APPLIER — "THE INBOUND UPDATE PATH MINTED NOTHING for jira/'admin' (bug 8d68): the applier
    still keys the mint on the scalar assignee string, which
    `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:105-106` rejects before reading any key".
  * CLOUD — "the Cloud inbound update did not mint under the accountId '5b10a2844c20165700ede21g'".
(An earlier attempt failed with a TypeError from passing `tracker_dir` as a str — an INVALID red,
proving nothing; it was fixed to a Path and re-run before the fix was written.) After the fix: 11
passed across the two 5200 modules.

CLOUD PROOF, which is the guard against the wrong fix. `test_the_cloud_update_path_keys_on_the_
account_id_not_the_display_name` drives the real differ + real applier phase with a Cloud-shaped
payload ({accountId: 5b10a2844c20165700ede21g, displayName: "Ada Lovelace"}) and asserts BOTH
that the mint registers under the accountId AND that `resolve_mapping("jira", "Ada Lovelace")`
is None. A fix that made the mint accept a bare string passes on DC and FAILS here.

MUTATION VERDICTS — two, each reverting one half, each failing for the right reason (all
AssertionError; no AttributeError/ImportError):
  * revert the DIFFER's forwarding -> 4 failed / 3 passed. Differ cell: "the inbound differ
    emitted an assignee change WITHOUT `assignee_identity`..."; contract cell: "the differ
    forwarded None, which is not the mapper's canonical identity {'display': 'Administrator',
    'email': 'admin@example.com', 'account_id': 'admin'}"; both applier cells red downstream.
  * revert the APPLIER's keying -> 2 failed / 5 passed, and the differ cell STAYS GREEN — the
    two boundaries are independently pinned, so a regression names which half broke.

ONE EXISTING ASSERTION INVERTED, intent preserved and recorded in its docstring: the diagnosis
module's `test_the_mapper_already_carries_everything_the_mint_needs` asserted
`"assignee_identity" not in changed` to pin the DROP as the mechanism. It now asserts the
forwarded value EQUALS the mapper's own canonical identity — same intent ("the mint's input comes
from the mapper, not from a re-derivation"), stated positively. No other test changed.

NO OTHER BEHAVIOUR MOVED: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/{diffing,conflict,mutate} 676 passed;
tests/integration/rebar_reconciler 35 passed; a full tests/unit + tests/integration run is in
flight. `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` produces no diff (neither file reads env).

MODULE SIZES: inbound_differ.py 706 -> 718; apply_inbound_records.py 565 -> 579. Both well under
the 800 cap.

REMAINING: a live harness run to confirm J11's
`test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity` goes green with no assertion weakened.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
EVIDENCE FOR THE TWO UNMET CLOSE CRITERIA. The first is a case where the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION
ANTICIPATED A DIFFERENT (AND WORSE) FIX SHAPE than the one implemented; the second is genuinely
outstanding and in flight.

=== CRITERION 1: 'cells 2 and 4 invert'. CELL 4 DID INVERT. CELL 2 MUST NOT, AND THAT IS THE FIX
WORKING AS DESIGNED — NOT AN OMISSION. ===

Cell 2 is test_the_mint_is_a_no_op_on_the_shape_the_update_path_hands_it, and it still asserts
    rebar.resolve_mapping('jira', _DC_USER, repo_root=store) is None
i.e. that _ensure_inbound_assignee_identity STILL mints nothing when handed a BARE STRING.

THAT ASSERTION IS CORRECT AFTER THE FIX, because the fix does not change what the mint accepts — it
changes WHAT THE CALLER HANDS IT. The mint's dict guard at _ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:105-106
('if not isinstance(assignee, dict): return') is DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED. The defect was never that
the guard existed; it was that inbound_differ dropped the canonical  the mapper
had already computed, so the applier had only the scalar to pass. The fix restores the identity at
the source: the differ now forwards , and the applier keys on
.

INVERTING CELL 2 WOULD REQUIRE MAKING THE MINT ACCEPT A BARE STRING — WHICH IS THE ONE FIX THAT WAS
EXPLICITLY PROHIBITED, and for a concrete reason. On Data Center the scalar happens to be 
(== the external id), so a string-accepting mint LOOKS correct there. On CLOUD the scalar is the
DISPLAY NAME, so minting keyed on it would register every Cloud user under the wrong id — turning a
silent no-op into silent DATA CORRUPTION, which is strictly worse than the bug being fixed. That is
why the prohibition was a hard constraint on this work and why cell 2 keeps its polarity: it is now
the REGRESSION GUARD against that wrong fix, pinned by a test instead of holding by accident.

CELL 4 DID INVERT, as the criterion expects: test_the_mapper_already_carries_everything_the_mint_needs
previously pinned '"assignee_identity" not in changed' as the defect's mechanism, and now asserts
the forwarded value equals the mapper's own canonical identity. Its intent is preserved and the
reason is recorded in its docstring.

THE CLOUD GUARD IS THE INDEPENDENT PROOF THAT THE CHOSEN SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE:
test_the_cloud_update_path_keys_on_the_account_id_not_the_display_name drives the real differ and the
real applier phase with {accountId: 5b10a2844c20165700ede21g, displayName: 'Ada Lovelace'} and
asserts the mint registers under the ACCOUNT ID and that resolve_mapping('jira', 'Ada Lovelace') is
None. A string-accepting fix passes on DC and FAILS that cell. So the two cells together encode the
distinction the criterion was reaching for.

MUTATION EVIDENCE that both boundaries are independently pinned (so nothing is passing vacuously):
reverting the differ's forwarding -> 4 failed / 3 passed; reverting ONLY the applier's keying -> 2
failed / 5 passed WITH THE DIFFER CELL STILL GREEN. All AssertionError, no AttributeError/ImportError.

=== CRITERION 2: the J11 live cell. GENUINELY OUTSTANDING, RUN IN FLIGHT. ===
test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity needs a harness run on a tree containing this
fix, with NO weakening of its assertions. Status:
 * the fix merged as ff7a761267 (Gerrit 1232), and its RED-first companion as c83263b7d4 (1231);
 * harness run **30772461871** was dispatched against main @ bd3de0f864, which contains both;
 * the oracle itself is UNCHANGED by this ticket — it is exactly as it landed in 1226/1227, so a
   green there cannot come from a relaxed assertion. That is the point: the cell was failing because
   the PRODUCT was wrong, and this ticket fixed the product.
The previous run (30767546938, main @ d72c4777d3, pre-fix) failed that cell with 'THE PASS MINTED
NOTHING', so the pair of runs will be a controlled before/after rather than a bare green.
DO NOT close this ticket until that run reports the cell PASSED — and read the per-cell verdict plus
the '[jira-live-canary] collected=N executed=N skipped=0' line, not the pass/fail count.

comments.body:
CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS COMMENT — three sentences lost their content to shell backtick
substitution when I posted it. The argument is unchanged; these are the missing specifics, which are
the load-bearing ones. (Recording a correction rather than leaving a comment with holes in exactly
the places that state what the fix does.)

1. WHERE IT SAYS "the differ now forwards , and the applier keys on ." — the full sentence is:
   the differ now forwards assignee_identity, and the applier keys on
       fields.get("assignee_identity") or fields["assignee"]
   The "or fields[...]" raw-object fallback is deliberate: it keeps differ-BYPASSING callers (which
   pass the raw Jira user object, a dict) working unchanged, so the fix adds a path without removing
   one. The mint then reads account_id after accountId/name, falling back to display.

2. WHERE IT SAYS "On Data Center the scalar happens to be (== the external id)" — the full sentence
   is: on Data Center the scalar happens to be name (== the external id), so a string-accepting mint
   LOOKS correct there. On Cloud the scalar is the DISPLAY NAME, which is why a string-accepting mint
   would register every Cloud user under the wrong id.

3. The dropped clause in the defect description: inbound_differ dropped the canonical
   assignee_identity that inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields:223-225 had ALREADY computed —
   the mapper emits both the scalar assignee string and the fixed-shape assignee_identity
   ({display, email, account_id}), and only the scalar was in field_map, so the applier had nothing
   else to pass.

Nothing else in that comment was affected: the cell-2/cell-4 reasoning, the prohibition rationale,
the Cloud-guard description, the mutation counts (4 failed/3 passed and 2 failed/5 passed with the
differ cell green), and the criterion-2 harness status are all intact as written.

compiled_state.description:
The inbound UPDATE path never mints an identity for an inbound assignee: it hands the mint a
bare STRING, and the mint's first line requires a dict. The mint returns immediately and
silently, because it is best-effort by contract. The inbound CREATE path is unaffected, which
is exactly why this has gone unseen.

FOUND BY: J11's live cell `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity`
(tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py) on harness run 30767546938, job 91548842532,
main @ d72c4777d3 — the first run in which that cell's precondition held and it reached its real
assertion. 48 passed / 1 failed, `[jira-live-canary] collected=49 executed=49 skipped=0`.

    AssertionError: THE PASS MINTED NOTHING: jira/'admin' still resolves to no identity in the
    store copy after an inbound pass that carried that assignee.

MECHANISM — PROVEN, NOT INFERRED. Each link is cited, and the chain is reproduced harness-free
in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py` (4 cells, green):

  1. `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields:223-225` maps the Jira user object to TWO
     canonical keys — the scalar `assignee` (a bare string from `_extract_jira_field_value`:
     `name`, else `displayName`) and the fixed-shape `assignee_identity`
     ({display, email, account_id}), whose `account_id` ALREADY carries Data Center's username
     (`_identity_of:154-179`, the precedence 5f48 established).
  2. `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local:185-188` emits ONLY the scalar:
     `changed["assignee"] = jira_mapped.get("assignee")`. `assignee_identity` is not in
     `field_map` (`:170-176`), so it never reaches the mutation.
  3. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_write_edit_event:333-340` states that these fields
     ARE the differ's local-keyed shape, and `:369` passes `fields["assignee"]` — that string —
     into `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity`.
  4. `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity:100-101` opens with
     `if not isinstance(assignee, dict): return`. A string returns before any key is read.
     Nothing is minted and nothing is logged: `:83-102` documents the function as
     "ADDITIVE + best-effort ... any mint failure is swallowed".

  The CREATE path at `:200-203` passes the RAW user object out of the snapshot, which IS a
  dict, so an inbound create mints correctly. Every identity the J11 harness has ever produced
  came from that path — including the one that made this cell's ORIGINAL precondition fail.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SETUP ARTIFACT OF THE CELL. The suspicion was that the cell's unassign/sync
step leaves the pass with no assignee CHANGE to act on. It does not: cell 1 of the reproduction
runs the real `_diff_jira_vs_local` with a local ticket that is unassigned and a Jira issue
assigned to admin — precisely the state the cell arranges — and the differ DOES emit
`changed["assignee"]`. So the mint is reached; it declines the value it is given.

WHY IT IS NOT A REGRESSION OF 5f48-244c-7063-42d0. That bug fixed the KEY SELECTION inside the
mint (`for key in ("accountId", "name")`) so a DC user object resolves. This defect is upstream
of that guard: on the update path the function returns at line 100 before any key is read, so
5f48's fix is never reached. It is a case 5f48 never covered.

SCOPE. The differ and the applier are deployment-neutral, so Cloud has the same gap on the
update path; DC ships it, which is why it belongs to this epic (e369's standing precedent for
defects in paths DC ships). Its practical effect: a user first seen on an inbound EDIT (rather
than on the issue's inbound create) never gets a ghost identity, so a later outbound pass has
nothing to key on — the exact failure mode 2f13's ghost-minting exists to prevent.

PROPOSED FIX (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — needs sign-off; no src/ change has been made).
Plumb the identity through instead of loosening the guard:
  * `inbound_differ._diff_jira_vs_local` — when it emits an `assignee` change, ALSO forward
    `jira_mapped["assignee_identity"]` (the mapper already computes it, at no extra extraction);
  * `apply_inbound_records:369` — key the mint on that canonical identity's `account_id` /
    `display` rather than on the scalar.
DO NOT "fix" this by making `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` accept a bare string. On Data
Center the scalar happens to be `name` (== the external id), so it would look correct here; on
Cloud the scalar is the DISPLAY NAME, and minting keyed on it would register every Cloud user
under the wrong external id — a silent data defect strictly worse than the missing mint.
The reproduction's 4th cell pins the contract a correct fix must meet.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
  * An inbound pass that carries an assignee CHANGE (not only an inbound create) mints/reuses a
    placeholder identity under the shared `jira` family, keyed on the deployment's external id
    (accountId on Cloud, username on DC), and NOT under `jira-datacenter`.
  * `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_inbound_update_assignee_mint_5200.py` is updated so the
    update path is proven to mint and the differ is proven to forward the identity, and cell 3
    stays green so the create path is shown not to regress. CRITERION AMENDED AFTER
    IMPLEMENTATION, and the reason matters: this originally read "cells 2 and 4 invert". Cell 4
    (`test_the_mapper_already_carries_everything_the_mint_needs`) DID invert. **Cell 2
    (`test_the_mint_is_a_no_op_on_the_shape_the_update_path_hands_it`) MUST NOT INVERT**, because
    inverting it would mean asserting that `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` ACCEPTS a bare
    string — the one fix this ticket explicitly prohibits, since on DC the scalar is `name`
    (== the external id) and looks right, while on Cloud it is the DISPLAY NAME and would
    register every Cloud user under the wrong id. The implemented fix keeps the mint's dict guard
    untouched and repairs the CALLER instead, so cell 2 correctly keeps its polarity and now
    serves as the regression guard against that wrong fix. The forward behaviour is proven by
    NEW cells (5-7) plus the Cloud accountId guard below. The original wording prescribed a
    mechanism that would have introduced the defect it was meant to prevent; the intent — "the
    update path mints; the differ forwards the identity" — is unchanged and is met.
  * A Cloud-shaped payload ({accountId, displayName} with displayName != accountId) mints keyed
    on the accountId — the guard against the wrong fix above.
  * The J11 live cell `test_the_inbound_assignee_mints_a_jira_family_identity` goes green on a
    harness run WITHOUT any weakening of its assertions.
